purpose: Canonical proxy-relative request routes for the five Critical request classes fired by the external evidence-mode workload driver (scripts/e6-workload-driver.mjs) against the real loopback Setjoin gateway stack stood up by scripts/e6-gateway-fixture.sh. The driver consumes this via E6_DRIVER_CLASS_ROUTES (JSON { [class]: { method, path } }, path proxy-relative, may carry a ${seq} token; an absolute URL is refused). Consumed verbatim: scripts/e6-gateway-fixture.sh emits the E6_DRIVER_CLASS_ROUTES env assignment from this file.

methodMapping.summary: Each class maps to the authoritative request path its client implementation actually uses. queued-send and draft-commit are JMAP methods carried by POST /jmap (the E4-I coordinator's sync/delta/window path is the same endpoint); their distinguishing request shape is the class body pinned in E6_DRIVER_CLASS_BODIES (emitted per member by the fixture). auth-revocation is the offline coordinator's revocation-flow request (installWipeHandler ack). security-state is the security-posture read the settings/security surface loads. delivery-receipt is the RFC 3798 MDN consent POST. Every route is requireAuth (driver Bearer) and repeatable at the >=1,000-completed-observations-per-class-per-run floor: submission/receipt/wipe-ack are idempotent by reducer contract, draft-commit and security-score are non-conflicting.
methodMapping.repeatabilityContract: The sustained schedule fires each class 1,000+ times per member run with ONE bearer token. POST /auth/logout and POST /user/sessions/revoke-all revoke all tokens on first fire and are therefore NOT usable as sustained routes; the pinned paths keep the Critical semantics on the same authoritative surfaces without self-destructing the run.
methodMapping.corpusBinding: queued-send submits the seeded per-member draft (messages.id 5400000001 / 5400000002) with onSuccessUpdateEmail present so the draft survives every send; delivery-receipt acknowledges the seeded receipt-requested corpus message (messages.id 5000000001 / 5100000001); auth-revocation acks the seeded per-member device (user_devices.device_id 5220000001 / 5220000002); draft-commit creates into the member's Drafts tag. All ids are fixed by scripts/e6-fixture/seed-corpus.sql and restored identically by reset-pair.

queued-send.body: E6_DRIVER_CLASS_BODIES[class] (fixture-emitted): JMAP EmailSubmission/set create {emailId: <seeded draft>, onSuccessUpdateEmail: {}}
authoritativeSource: mailserver/sql/reducers/jmap_email_submission.sql — jmap_email_submission_set (send -> deliver, onSuccessUpdateEmail keeps the draft)

draft-commit.body: E6_DRIVER_CLASS_BODIES[class] (fixture-emitted): JMAP Email/set create {mailboxIds: {<drafts tag id>: true}, from/to, subject, bodyValues}

authoritativeSource: mailserver/webmail/src/lib/offline/wipe.ts — installWipeHandler ack POST /api/offline/wipe-ack (keepalive, the coordinator-owned request of the auth/revocation flow)
mailserver/internal/user/devices.go — WipeAck: BZ101 (no pending wipe) is idempotent 200
mailserver/sql/reducers/offline_device_wipe_ack.sql — R3 ownership in the same UPDATE

operationalNotes: Routes are proxy-relative gateway paths: /jmap and /auth/* are gateway top-level; /api/* is the gateway's StripPrefix('/api') mount (the golden inventory records post-strip patterns).
The class mix (20% each) and the schedule are owned by the frozen profile and the harness buildPlan; this file pins only the request shapes.
Bodies are account-scoped and therefore fixture-emitted per member, not frozen here: the corpus ids they reference are deterministic (seed-corpus.sql) and survive reset-pair identically.
Any change to a path here requires a route_inventory.golden match plus a new profileVersion for any results already qualified.
